subject: Materials Science
title: Intergranular Corrosion
description: A quick, practical guide to Intergranular Corrosion.

hook.text: A stainless steel weld falls apart along grain boundaries — the grains are fine but the borders are dissolved.

buildup.text: Intergranular corrosion attacks grain boundaries preferentially — leaving grains intact but disconnected.

discovery.text: In stainless steel, heating to 450–850°C depletes chromium at grain boundaries — sensitization.

twist.text: The chromium-depleted zones lose their passive film — they become anodes surrounded by cathodic grain interiors.

climax.text: Low-carbon stainless steels (304L, 316L) resist sensitization — the 'L' stands for low carbon.

punchline.text: Guard the grain boundaries and the whole structure stays connected.

quiz.question: What causes sensitization in stainless steel?
options: Excessive cold working of the metal
Chromium depletion at grain boundaries due to heating
